captions.detailed: This 3D model presents a flat-pack, 3D-printable glasses frame assembly consisting of three major components laid out flat on the build plate. The main frame features a rectangular dual-lens rim design connected by a central nose bridge, complete with raised hinge blocks at the outer edges. Positioned alongside the frame are two straight temple arms with curved ear hooks and matching hinge connectors. Two small cylindrical pin tacks are also included on the print bed to serve as the hinge pivot pins.
captions.instruction: Design a parametric, 3D-printable glasses frame with folding temple arms in OpenSCAD. The script should allow users to customize the frame width, lens shape (round or square), frame thickness, temple length, and include functional hinge blocks that use printable pivot pins.
captions.factory: The script defines the glasses frame using a difference() operation between outer shapes (using 'roundedBox' or 'oval' modules) and subtracted lens openings. The central bridge is modeled with a simple cube, while the hinges are created using custom modules that incorporate difference() operations for horizontal pivot holes. The temple arms are constructed from combined cubes and a custom 'hook' shape, featuring corresponding hinge blocks with matching pinholes designed to accommodate pintack connectors.
